previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was readmitted one day after discharge due to shaking chills and worsening pain around his indwelling urinary catheter site. Initially treated for suspected sepsis with broad-spectrum antibiotics, he was found to have a urinary tract infection caused by E. coli and Serratia marcescens. After culture results, antibiotics were narrowed to IV ceftriaxone. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic administration. He also received treatment for bilateral conjunctivitis and facial impetigo. His symptoms improved, and he was discharged to short-term rehab to complete his antibiotic course and address deconditioning. Follow-up was arranged with urology, cardiology, and primary care.
problems: Urinary catheterization as the cause of abnormal reaction

CLINICAL HISTORY:  CAD, status post CABG, diabetes, presents with weakness,
assess pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  AP upright and lateral views of the chest are obtained.  Midline
sternotomy wires are again noted as well as mediastinal clips and stigmata of
prior CABG.  There is stable elevation of the left hemidiaphragm.  There is
linear atelectasis at the right lung base.  There is mild pulmonary vascular
congestion without frank pulmonary edema.  Calcified nodules project in the
left mid to upper lung.  The patient is known to have calcified pleural
plaque.  Heart size cannot be assessed.  Mediastinal contour is stable.  Bony
structures appear grossly intact.  Degenerative changes in the thoracic spine
noted.

IMPRESSION:  Mild pulmonary vascular congestion, bibasilar atelectasis.
